pages.text: Vinicius Jr: Real Madrid forward says transfer interest has affected form - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid in August By Marissa Thomas BBC Sport journalist Published 16 November 2026 Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season. The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season. He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real. The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup. "I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said. "Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years. "That may have affected my start to the season. "On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season." Mr. Hobbs held managerial and technical positions for nearly 20 years with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. His final assignment was the Hartwell Project Operations Manager with Savannah District. May 15, 2024 Español Vision Loss and Diabetes What to know Diabetes can damage your eyes over time and cause vision loss or blindness. Managing your diabetes can help to prevent or delay eye problems. Regular eye exams help to diagnose eye problems early so you can get treatment and protect your eyesight. Diabetic retinopathy Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of blindness in working-age adults. DR is when high blood sugar damages blood vessels in the retina (a part of your eye). Damaged blood vessels can swell and leak, causing blurry vision. DR usually affects both eyes. Diabetes can damage the small blood vessels at the back of the eyes, leading to vision loss. Risk factors Anyone with type 1, type 2, or gestational diabetes (diabetes while pregnant) can develop DR. The longer you have diabetes, the more likely you are to develop it. These factors can also increase your risk: High blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels. Smoking. Being an African American, Hispanic/Latino, or American Indian or Alaska Native person. pages.text: Visit Kuélap, a Peruvian Archaeological Site a Millennium Older Than Machu Picchu | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Visit Kuélap, a Peruvian Archaeological Site a Millennium Older Than Machu Picchu The remote region north of Lima is also a paradise for lovers of mummies, wildlife, and orchids. At more than 2,500 feet, the Gocta waterfall, near the village of Cocachimba in northern Peru, is one of the world’s tallest. Ernesto Benavides By Heather Jasper Published October 20, 2026 Although the pre-Incan fortress of Kuélap is almost a thousand years older than Machu Picchu, it gets only a fraction of the crowds. The Chachapoya people built the citadel in northern Peru around the year 500 A.D. on a narrow fin of limestone high above the Utcubamba River—not unlike Machu Picchu’s perch above the Vilcanota River. Visit in 2027 to see new exhibits in the Apu Chuillaxa visitors’ center and walk a new trail in Malcapampa , an active archaeological site that has been newly opened to the public. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) When to Go The warm, rainy season arrives in the cloud forests of this part of Peru in November and lasts until April. More than a thousand orchid species are in bloom and the waterfalls thunder with extra volume. A cooler dry season from May through October offers better road conditions and drier trails, making it easier to visit archaeological sites around Kuélap. Here’s what the experts say about vitamin A and E. By Daryl Austin Last updated April 2, 2025 Vitamins and supplements are a booming industry. And while there are many important supplements that benefit people with specific deficiencies or certain health conditions, research shows and experts agree that some synthetic vitamins could cause harms such as liver damage, hair loss, joint and muscle pain, and impaired vision. "Everyone is always searching for that magic pill that will give them great health, but dietary supplements just aren't it because the benefits often don't outweigh the risks," says JoAnn Manson, chief of preventive medicine at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. pages.text: Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s single hits piece of broken bat Skip to Content Talk about getting the barrel on it. Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. technically squared up his RBI single in the seventh inning of Friday's 6-5 win over the Reds at Rogers Centre, but he did it in quite an unusual way. On an 0-2 sinker from Cincinnati reliever Luis Mey, Guerrero chopped a ground ball toward the middle, breaking his bat in the process. Then, pure baseball magic took over. Slow-motion replay showed exactly what happened: The severed barrel of Guerrero's bat connected with the baseball several feet in front of home plate, redirecting the ball toward the right side of the infield. It rolled through a hole in the Reds' defense and into right field for a single, scoring Andrés Giménez from second base. Guerrero's hit, which brought in the first run of a pivotal four-run seventh to give Toronto the lead and eventually the win, was far from the first base hit on which a player hit the ball twice. In fact, it was at least the sixth this season -- including two on the same day. While it surely wasn't the hard contact Guerrero envisioned, Friday's double-hit allowed him to "hit 'em where they ain't" in a truly ingenious way.

Voices of Experience The Office of Electricity (OE) pioneered the Voices of Experience (Voices) approach more than a decade ago in response to industry feedback. The Voices efforts convene stakeholders to facilitate peer-to-peer sharing, with conversations focused on technologies and emerging issues facing industry. By actively listening to these conversations, OE gains a greater understanding of how technologies and concepts are being implemented and deployed, helping to identify gaps or barriers that can hinder progress. A Unique Approach The Voices of Experience approach is unique from other DOE stakeholder engagement efforts. It uses the art of the question and a structured approach that is centered on open dialogue and active listening to gather firsthand insights. Discussions include a mix of multi-stakeholder and single-stakeholder conversations, allowing for cross-pollination of ideas as well as safe spaces for more candid discussions. They like exploring tight dark places, undeterred by mud and whatever may be lurking. Give a caver a task to do, while down in a cave’s depths, and they will stay underground for hours and come back again a few weeks later to do it again. As it turns out, these are the same unique qualities found in some of the Bureau of Land Management’s most remarkable volunteers. The Bureau recently recognized one, in particular, with this year’s BLM Outstanding Volunteer Achievement Award. Carrin Rich from Carnuel, New Mexico, led cave restoration work at the Fort Stanton-Snowy River Cave National Conservation Area, along with a team of more than two-dozen volunteer cavers from New Mexico and Texas. Who to contact about voter accommodations If you know you will need accommodations to vote in person on Election Day, contact your state or local election office . They can help you understand what to expect at your polling place. Laws and accommodations for voters with disabilities Several federal laws protect the voting rights of Americans with disabilities. These include the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the Help America Vote Act (HAVA) . Voters with disabilities have the right to: Vote in private, without help Have an accessible polling place with voting machines for voters with disabilities Polling places must have: Wheelchair-accessible voting booths Entrances and doorways at least 32 inches wide Handrails on all stairs Voting equipment for people who are blind or visually impaired If you have a disability, you may: Seek help from poll workers trained to use an accessible voting machine, or Bring someone to help you vote You can also ask your state or local election office what other options you have. Some states offer “curbside voting," when a poll worker brings everything you need to vote to your car. Local organizations may provide transportation to the polls. pages.text: Voter ID requirements | USAGov Skip to main content Voter ID requirements Each state sets its own voter ID rules. And most require voters to bring identification to vote in person. Know the voter ID laws in your state before going to the polls. Find out if you need to bring an ID to vote Your state's voter ID laws determine whether you will need to show an ID and, if so, what kind. Your state may require you to show a photo ID like a: Driver's license State ID Passport They may ask to see another form of identification like your birth certificate, or Social Security card. If you are a registered voter and have a voter registration card, you are not required to bring it with you when you vote. But you can still use it as a form of identification. Find out what ID your state requires you to bring when you vote. Or learn how to get a voter registration card . How to vote without ID if you are eligible Even if you do not have a form of ID that your state asks for, you may be able to vote. Some states may ask you to sign a form affirming your identity. Find out if you can vote in your state without ID and what information you may need to provide when you vote. Other states will let you cast a provisional ballot. States use provisional ballots when there is a question about a voter's eligibility. They keep your provisional ballot separate until they investigate your eligibility. You may have to return to show an acceptable form of ID within a few days, or the ballot will not count. Learn more about provisional ballots and if you may need to cast one in your state. Learn about the laws and how they protect your rights and make it easier for you to vote. U.S. election laws date back to Article 1 of the Constitution. This gave states the responsibility of overseeing federal elections. Many constitutional amendments and federal laws protecting voting rights have been passed since then. Constitutional amendments affecting voting rights The 15th Amendment gave African American men the right to vote in 1870. But many weren't able to exercise this right. Some states used literacy tests and other barriers to make it harder to vote. The 19th Amendment , ratified in 1920, gave American women the right to vote. The 24th Amendment , ratified in 1964, eliminated poll taxes. The tax had been used in some states to keep African Americans from voting in federal elections. The 26th Amendment , ratified in 1971, lowered the voting age for all elections to 18. That is how former captain Sam Warburton described the monumental result against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday. At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top-ranked side in the world following South Africa's tension-filled loss to France on Friday night. So no-one gave Wales a glimmer of hope - even Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30-1 during the week. The question, not of when but can Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset them since 1953. That 73-year wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy, tears and relief to the strains of Yma O Hyd. Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff. Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins. The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes. Prop Archie Griffin also added a first-half try, but New Zealand responded with scores from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, number eight Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo to level the score 21-21 at half-time. Wales centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit scored early second-half tries before New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai pulled one back. pages.text: Wales beat New Zealand: Replacements show tackling prowess in Nations Championship win - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Ben Carter and Gareth Thomas are part of Wales' 39-man squad for the Nations Championship By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 18 November 2026 They say rugby is now a game that relies on 23 players. There was ample evidence of that during Wales' remarkable 35-28 win against New Zealand last Saturday. The headline acts were the 346 tackles made by the team, which was a world record for an international match. The 38 tackles managed by lock Dafydd Jenkins matched the top individual tally, while Jac Morgan (31), James Botham (30), Eddie James (25), captain Dewi Lake (24) and Max Llewellyn (23) were not far behind. It was the impact of the bench that also proved crucial in the defensive stand of the final quarter. Replacement back rower Taine Plumtree popped up with two crucial turnovers, while Gareth Thomas and Ben Carter made a combined 32 tackles in 42 minutes. Ospreys prop Thomas managed 19 in 26 minutes, while lock Carter's return was 13 in 16 minutes to add to the remarkable statistics and contributions. pages.text: Wales v Australia: Five key areas for Steve Tandy's side to back up All Blacks win - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Despite beating New Zealand and Japan this November, Wales lie fifth of the six teams in the Nations Championship Northern Hemisphere table By Matt Lloyd BBC Sport Wales Published 17 November 2026 As the dust settles on Wales' historic victory over New Zealand, work is under way to secure another major scalp. Steve Tandy's side ensured their place in history by ending the 73-year wait for a win against the All Blacks. Now they must back up what many are describing as the one of the greatest results in Welsh rugby history by beating Australia in Cardiff on Saturday. Wales have won just one of their past five meetings with the Wallabies and are without a victory over them in Cardiff since 2021. But victory would complete only their second ever clean sweep of autumn internationals following the statement win on Saturday. "[Beating the All Blacks] wasn't even by fluke, that's the nicest thing," former Wales centre Tom Shanklin told the Scrum V podcast. "It wasn't like there were two or three cards for New Zealand. Wales did it the hard way and deserved to win." So what must Wales get right this week on the final weekend of the Nations Championship group stage? pages.text: Wales v Australia: Steve Tandy's squad witness Wales delight but turn attention to Australia - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Wales won their first three games against New Zealand but have had to wait 73 years for a fourth By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 17 November 2026 Wales' battered and bruised rugby heroes have been using the reaction of the nation to help soothe their aches and pains as they prepare for their next challenge. Steve Tandy's squad came back to training on Monday, 48 hours after their famous 35-28 win saw them become the first Wales side to defeat the All Blacks since 1953. Wales had celebrated the victory on Saturday night, and the squad assembled as a whole a little later on Monday than in previous weeks as attention now turns to facing Australia this Saturday in Cardiff. There was a video shown during one of the team meetings about what the All Blacks victory meant to fans. "The players came in a bit later on Monday after being given a bit of time off to enjoy the feeling with their families," said Wales assistant coach Matt Sherratt. "We kind of reviewed the New Zealand game yesterday, but let the lads enjoy it as well. "That was powerful in terms of the reaction from friends, families and the country as a whole. "The group deserved to feel that yesterday also and we showed them what it meant to the country. "The boys loved watching some of the videos we've seen, some of the memes online about people's reactions in their living rooms. That's what it's all about." The Junction Trail starts at the park visitor center and covers the area where Jubal Early's Confederate forces deployed to attack the bridge at the river below. The Gambrill Mill area includes an accessible boardwalk to a view of the Monocacy River where Union forces put up a desperate defense. The Worthington Farm area is where Confederate forces crossed the river to flank the Union forces, and the Thomas Farm was hotly contested ground during the battle. Each of these farms has its own story as well; Best Farm was once the home to over 100 enslaved people and one of the largest plantations in Maryland. pages.text: Washington's Trials, Lesson 4 | Crash Course: American Revolution | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE CRASH COURSE Washington’s Trials Lesson 4: Defeated in New York and pursued by redcoats, a beleaguered continental army triumphed at Trenton—and revived the revolutionary cause. By the time the United States declared independence on July 4, 1776 , Washington’s army was in New York City, anticipating a British invasion. New York was home to many British loyalists, or Tories, but some had fled and others were lying low to avoid harassment by American revolutionaries. New York’s royal governor, William Tryon, had taken refuge offshore on a British sloop of war in October 1775 and plotted to assassinate Washington, a scheme exposed in June 1776 . Patriots infuriated by the plot went after suspected Tories and scourged them. One witness saw men “being carried through the streets on rails, their clothes tore from their back and their bodies pretty well mingled with the dust.” Shortly after the Declaration of Independence was read in the city, 40 colonial soldiers and sailors celebrated by hauling down a large-scale gilded lead statue of King George III on horseback at the city’s Bowling Green park, severing the head, and sending parts of the statue to Connecticut, where the metal was recast to form musket balls for Washington’s forces. pages.description: When the National Geographic Society needed an enormous new globe for the atrium of the new Museum of Exploration, they called on one of the few companies capable of crafting one by hand.
pages.text: Watch artisans craft Nat Geo's enormous new handmade globe | National Geographic Video by Dominic Howlett Text by Halley Brown Published June 22, 2026 0:26 On a cloudy day in central London, artisans at Bellerby & Co, Globemakers are putting the finishing touches on the largest handcrafted globe they’ve ever made. Over the previous few months, every plateau, peninsula, island, and mountain ridge on Earth had been painstakingly hand-painted on the five foot diameter 100-pound sphere. Today, a final coat of watercolor paint is laid on, but then, a new challenge arises: how to get it out of the studio. The completed globe is so large that it doesn’t fit through the front door. Instead, a crane plucks the globe, now placed in a shipment crate, from the studio’s roof and sets it in the quiet alleyway, where it starts a transatlantic journey to be installed at the new National Geographic Museum of Exploration, opening this week. Much about traditional globe making hasn’t changed since the 16th century. But Bellerby & Co is a relative newcomer to the craft. In 2008, owner Peter Bellerby was working in real estate when he went searching for a handcrafted globe for his father’s 80th birthday. His only options were either purchasing an expensive antique, so fragile it couldn’t be touched, or a mass-produced globe riddled with geographic errors. He couldn’t find a company making one-off bespoke globes. 0:11 He decided to make two globes on his own, immersing himself in the meticulous craft. pages.description: While the kea parrot’s beak would normally be considered essential for survival, Bruce has innovated other ways of commanding respect.
pages.text: Watch Bruce the parrot defeat his rivals with only half a beak | National Geographic ANIMALS Watch Bruce the parrot defeat his rivals with only half a beak While the kea parrot’s beak would normally be considered essential for survival, Bruce has innovated other ways of commanding respect. Bruce the kea parrot lost his upper beak, but his disability hasn't stemmed his curiosity. He has become the alpha male in his group. Video: Alex Grabham By Jack Tamisiea Published April 20, 2026 Kea parrots are known for being extremely curious and capable of solving complex problems ; they can even make each other chuckle . Now, for the first time, a kea named Bruce has demonstrated skilled combat techniques after losing his upper beak. Despite missing a facial feature thought to be crucial for survival, Bruce has worked his way to becoming the alpha male of his circus, the collective noun for a group of kea, at the Willowbank Wildlife Reserve in Christchurch, New Zealand. These olive-green parrots have fiery orange feathers under their wings and live in the mountains of New Zealand’s South Island. To determine how Bruce achieved such a high social standing even with a physical impediment, a team of researchers recently analyzed how Bruce interacted with other males in his group. Their findings, published in the journal Current Biology , reveal that Bruce uses a novel jousting-like attack with his feet and lower beak to vanquish rivals. “I think it’s very clear that Bruce has made the most of his half-beak,” says Amalia Bastos , a comparative psychologist at the University of St. Andrew

Watch Live: The 2025 NEA Jazz Masters tribute concert April 25, 2025 2:20 PM ET From Nate Chinen YouTube The NEA Jazz Masters fellowship began in 1982, establishing a lifetime achievement honor for practitioners of a uniquely American art form. One of the first three inductees was Sun Ra — a composer, bandleader and keyboardist whose frame of reference transcended earthbound restrictions, let alone national borders. Over the ensuing four decades, the NEA Jazz Masters program has continued to recognize artists and advocates whose influence circles the globe. Marshall Allen, who has held down the alto saxophone chair in the Sun Ra Arkestra since the mid-1950s, is the senior member of the new class of NEA Jazz Masters, bringing the honor full circle. Allen has led the Arkestra since shortly after Sun Ra's earthly departure in 1993. Now a centenarian, he was recently certified the "oldest person to release a debut album (male)" by Guinness World Records, and remains a vibrant performer as well as a link to cosmic history.
